questions.stem:
The function f is defined by
$\mathrm{f}: x \mapsto \frac{5x+1}{x^2+x-2}-\frac{3}{x+2}$, $x>1$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{2}{x-1}$, $x>1$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: $\frac{5x+1}{(x+2)(x-1)}-\frac{3}{x+2}$
M1: $=\frac{5x+1-3(x-1)}{(x+2)(x-1)}$ (M1 for combining fractions even if the denominator is not lowest common)
M1 A1 cso: $=\frac{2x+4}{(x+2)(x-1)}=\frac{2(x+2)}{(x+2)(x-1)}=\frac{2}{x-1}$ * (M1 must have linear numerator)

parts.label: b(i)
parts.text:
(b) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(i) M1A1: $y=\frac{2}{x-1} \Rightarrow xy-y=2 \Rightarrow xy=2+y$
A1: $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{2+x}{x}$ o.e.

questions.question_text:
A particular species of orchid is being studied. The population $p$ at time $t$ years after the study started is assumed to be

Given that there were 300 orchids when the study started,
(a) show that $a=0.12$,
(3)
(b) use the equation with $a=0.12$ to predict the number of years before the population of orchids reaches 1850.
(4)
(c) Show that $p=\frac{336}{0.12+\mathrm{e}^{-0.2t}}$.
(1)
(d) Hence show that the population cannot exceed 2800.
(2)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) M1: Setting $p=300$ at $t=0 \Rightarrow 300=\frac{2800a}{1+a}$
dM1A1: $(300=2500a)$; $a=0.12$ (c.s.o.)
(b) M1A1: $1850=\frac{2800(0.12)\mathrm{e}^{0.2t}}{1+0.12\mathrm{e}^{0.2t}}$; $\mathrm{e}^{0.2t}=16.2…$
M1: Correctly taking logs to $0.2t=\ln k$
A1: $t=14$ $(13.9..)$
(c) B1: Correct derivation: (Showing division of num. and den. by $\mathrm{e}^{0.2t}$; using $a$)
(d) M1: Using $t \to \infty$, $\mathrm{e}^{-0.2t} \to 0$
A1: $p \to \frac{336}{0.12}=2800$
